summary: Proposes an alternative to IPsec for securing signaling between a Mobile IPv6 mobile node and its home agent. It defines a mobility message authentication option that can be added to Binding Updates and Acknowledgements. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Instead of putting a whole armored truck around your messages, you sign each message with a seal. This memo proposes seals for messages between a moving device and its home base.

questions: what is mobile ipv6 authentication option
alternative to ipsec for mobile ipv6
how does mobile ipv6 replay protection work
subtitle: A lightweight, shared-key way to authenticate Mobile IPv6 signaling for networks that cannot use IPsec between phone and home agent.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv6 secures the Binding Update and Binding Acknowledgement messages between a Mobile Node and its Home Agent with IPsec. Some mobile networks assign home agents dynamically, lack IKEv2 support and want fewer signaling messages.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a mobility message authentication option, carrying a keyed hash computed with a shared key, plus an optional timestamp-based replay protection option. Both ride inside the Binding Update and Binding Acknowledgement.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational alternative for the specific networks described in its applicability statement, such as 3GPP2 networks. The IESG note says its security properties were not reviewed in the IETF and recommends against use outside those conditions.

today: RFC 4285 is Informational and has not been obsoleted or updated. Its own IESG note says it is not a candidate for any Internet Standard and that it should not be used outside the environments in its applicability statement. The standards-track mechanism remains in RFC 3775.

sections.title: Why an Alternative to IPsec
sections.content:
Base Mobile IPv6 (RFC 3775) secures the Binding Update (BU) and Binding Acknowledgement (BA) messages between a Mobile Node (MN) and its Home Agent (HA) with IPsec security associations. This RFC lets a node run Mobile IPv6 without establishing an IPsec security association with its Home Agent, and without integrating with the IPsec module.

The RFC's applicability statement lists the networks it is meant for: the Home Agent and home address are assigned dynamically, the only long-term security association is between the node and a backend AAA server, not every node and Home Agent supports IKEv2, and bandwidth is constrained so fewer signaling messages are wanted. CDMA networks are given as an example. The mechanism is similar to the one used in Mobile IPv4 (RFC 3344).

The IESG note says this RFC is not a candidate for any level of Internet Standard, its security properties have not been reviewed in the IETF, and the IESG recommends against using it outside environments that meet the applicability statement.
sections.eli5: Some phone networks cannot use the heavy security gear that is normally used. This memo offers a lighter lock for those networks only.

sections.title: Operational Flow
sections.content:
The Mobile Node sends a BU to the Home Agent (or the home AAA server, AAAH) that includes the Mobile Node Identifier option, an optional mobility message replay protection option and the mobility message authentication option. The Home Agent or AAAH authenticates the node and returns a BA carrying the same kinds of options.

The node MUST identify itself with the MN-NAI form of the Mobile Node Identifier option from RFC 4283. It MAY use the replay protection option for extra replay protection.

One limit is stated plainly: when these options are used, Return Routability messages are not protected for confidentiality, and Mobile Prefix Discovery is not authenticated or integrity protected. Unless the network guarantees such protection (as 3GPP2 networks do), Route Optimization and Mobile Prefix Discovery should not be used.
sections.eli5: The phone sends a note with its name tag and a seal. The home base checks the seal, then sends back a note that also has a seal.

sections.title: The Authentication Option
sections.content:
The mobility message authentication option has an Option Type, an Option Length, a Subtype, a Mobility SPI and variable Authentication Data. The Option Type value is 9 (AUTH-OPTION-TYPE). Its alignment requirement is 4n + 1. The Authentication Data protects the message from the Mobility Header up to and including the Mobility SPI field.

The Subtype says who authenticates the message. Subtype 1 is the MN-HA option, based on a shared key between the node and the Home Agent. Subtype 2 is the MN-AAA option, based on a shared key between the node and the home AAA server, and it is used only in Binding Updates.

For MN-HA, the shared-key security association holds a mobility SPI, a 16-octet key, the algorithm HMAC_SHA1 and the replay protection method. The data is the first 96 bits of HMAC_SHA1 over the care-of address, the home address and the Mobility Header content, with the Mobility Header Checksum set to 0. For MN-AAA with the well-known SPI HMAC_SHA1_SPI, the hash is computed over a SHA1 digest of the same data. The MN-HA option MUST be last if it is the only authentication option; if both appear, MN-HA comes first, otherwise the Home Agent MUST discard the message.
sections.eli5: The seal has a label saying who checks it and which secret key to use. The secret key is mixed with the message to make a short code, and the checker makes the same code to see if it matches.

sections.title: Failure Handling and Replay Protection
sections.content:
A BU or BA without the option, sent to a node configured to use it, should be silently discarded. If authentication fails and a shared-key security association exists, the Home Agent MUST send a BA with status code MIPV6-AUTH-FAIL. Without such an association it drops the BU and may log it. On receiving MIPV6-AUTH-FAIL the Mobile Node SHOULD stop sending new BUs.

The optional mobility message replay protection option (Option Type 10) carries a 64-bit NTP-format timestamp. The Home Agent checks it only after the BU is authenticated: the value must be close enough to its own clock and greater than all previously accepted timestamps for that node. A default window of 7 seconds MAY be used, and it SHOULD be greater than 3 seconds. If the timestamp is bad but authentication succeeded, the Home Agent sends a BA with MIPV6-ID-MISMATCH and creates no binding cache entry. The node then authenticates the BA, adjusts its timestamp and retries. If the policy requires this option and the BU lacks it, the Home Agent discards the BU and sets MIPV6-MESG-ID-REQD in the BA.
sections.eli5: If the seal is wrong, the home base says so and the phone stops pestering it. The date on each note keeps someone from re-sending an old note.

sections.title: Security and the Replay Rationale
sections.content:
The Security Considerations section is short: the new options authenticate BU and BA messages as an alternative to IPsec, and the MN-AAA option allows authentication through AAA infrastructure. Replay protection is optional, and the Sequence Number field in the BU is not used when it is in use.

Appendix A explains why timestamps are used. Base Mobile IPv6 lets a Home Agent with no binding cache entry accept any Sequence Number, so a replayed BU could create a binding. Because a node may use a different Home Agent each session, expecting every Home Agent to keep state is unreasonable. Having the Home Agent reject the first BU and assign a starting number would need an extra round trip, which is not acceptable in certain deployments.
sections.eli5: An old note could be replayed to trick the home base. A timestamp on each note lets the home base spot old ones without remembering every phone.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: IANA assigned option types 9 (AUTH-OPTION-TYPE) and 10 (MESG-ID-OPTION-TYPE) and three status codes. It also created a registry of algorithms indexed by mobility SPIs in the range 0-255 and a registry of subtypes for the authentication options. New values in both namespaces are allocated by IETF Consensus. SPI value 3 is reserved for HMAC_SHA1_SPI and value 5 for 3GPP2.
sections.eli5: The numbers for the new labels were handed out by the keeper of the official list, so nobody else uses the same ones.

messages.label: Binding Update
messages.note: MN-ID option, optional replay protection option, authentication option.

messages.label: Binding Acknowledgement
messages.note: Sent after the HA/AAAH authenticates the node; carries the same kinds of options.

items.label: MIPV6-ID-MISMATCH
items.desc: Authentication succeeded but the timestamp was not valid.

items.label: MIPV6-MESG-ID-REQD
items.desc: Policy requires the replay protection option and the BU lacked it.

items.label: MIPV6-AUTH-FAIL
items.desc: Authentication of the Binding Update failed.
